sentences.text: Morenosaurus was an extinct plesiosaur, a marine reptile with a long neck, that lived during the Cretaceous period in what is now California.
This animal lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago, just before the mass extinction event.
Robert Wallace and Arthur Drescher discovered the species in the Panoche Hills region of Fresno County. Samuel Welles named the species Morenosaurus stocki in 1943 to honor Dr. Chester Stock.

Morenosaurus is classified in the family Elasmosauridae, though this classification is uncertain. Studies in the early 2000s suggested that the Morenosaurus fossils were too fragmentary to definitively identify the animal to the family level.
Scientists debate whether the fragmentary fossils allow for a definitive family-level identification, leading to uncertainty about its exact classification within Elasmosauridae.
